chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir used to say to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May Allah have mercy on you, and by Allah, you know that if you took a dinar and the exchange rate was nineteen [fils], and you circulated throughout all of Medina seeking someone who would give you twenty [fils], you would not find him. And this is not but an escape [from reality]. And my father used to say, 'You are truthful, by Allah, but it is an escape from falsehood to truth.'

key_terms.دِينَار: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'escaping from falsehood to truth' mean in the context of Islamic economic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *firar min al-batil ila al-haqq* (escaping falsehood to truth) within the context of currency exchange (*sarf*). While the market rate represents the objective reality, seeking a disproportionate gain is viewed as a departure from equitable trade norms; the Imam’s father validates this by framing the pursuit of fair value as a transition from the 'falsehood' of market rigidity to the 'truth' of just compensation. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ethical economic conduct where intent and fairness align with divine justice.
